study.question: Observed limitation: stopped match-action rows improve validation over item-derived replacement, yet unrestricted within-block action rotation conflates historical click/nonclick association with distinctions among auxiliary feedback combinations. Does preserving the historical click bit during a count-matched conditional permutation preserve the match-summary utility, and does that contrast depend on task versus shared residual routing?
study.hypothesis: Provisional mechanism, not established: a substantial part of match-action alignment utility is carried by the association between a historical click bit and target-related advertisements. r0037 aligned stopped actions score0.6661693800 task/0.6646058218 shared; r0038 unrestricted rotation scores0.6637436112/0.6619771144, losses0.0024257689/0.0026287073. True historical-click strata preserve that bit at each event while shuffling any remaining within-class action distinctions. Count-matched shifted strata can destroy the bit association with equal group sizes and source-index movement. Predict true-stratum AUC exceeds shifted-stratum AUC; differences between task/shared contrasts localize operational dependence on routing. These are single-seed observations with uncertified host tensor diagnostics, not repeated mechanism support. The incumbent remains g0-r0022-support_rotated_attached at0.6667535475; no new predictive improvement is claimed.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary section4.3 lines250-277 verifies target-conditioned local activation and unnormalized intensity. Retain these components; add only a conditional-permutation diagnostic in already-existing downstream action summaries. Four-task compressed architecture is an adaptation, not exact DIN reproduction or a new attention method.

Pinned benchmark forward123-170 initializes per-task sequence hubs using supplied task masks and updates categorical/sequence/task representations. Here masks only define counterfactual grouping for two existing stopped summary rows; no hubs, broadcast layers or new parameters are introduced. Original INFNet paper mechanics and priority are not verified.

Pinned benchmark forward119-156 and block description158-163 use repeated sequence/nonsequence interaction, cross-attention and token FFNs. None is adopted: this experiment isolates historical action association at fixed architecture. No original-method equivalence or novelty claim.

study.proposed_difference: Four standalone modules cross partition semantics (true historical click vs count-matched shifted historical click membership) with existing task/shared residual routing. Intersect supplied historical is_click mask with original validity. In each original10-event block, shifted membership is the inherited half-valid-rank rotation, preserving positive/negative group counts. Separately rotate action embeddings by floor(group_count/2) within both groups, with empty/singleton identities. Apply the resulting stream only to action summary rows0/4 using inherited selectors; all other consumers keep original streams. No original event mask, feature visibility, target action, scorer population, bank width, gradient ownership or host recipe changes. Group sizes and number of moved source indices match exactly across semantic controls. This is an attribution study, not a new unified architecture; originality beyond inspected sources is unverified.
predictions: Primary paired contrasts D_task=AUC(true_task)-AUC(shifted_task), D_shared=AUC(true_shared)-AUC(shifted_shared); directional hypothesis both positive when artificial groups measurably disrupt historical click pairing. Treat a loss or null as a valid result.

Report D_task-D_shared as an operational routing interaction, with no prespecified sign: prior unrestricted-rotation losses differ by only about-0.000203 in this difference-of-differences. One seed cannot establish that small interaction.

Compare each true/shifted cell with the matching g1-r0037 aligned observed-stop and g1-r0038 unrestricted-rotation endpoint only after bridge certification. True closer to aligned than shifted is compatible with click-bit association utility. Remaining true-vs-aligned loss can implicate other action distinctions or intervention geometry, without establishing which auxiliary bit matters.

Training-only diagnostics should show equal group counts and index mobility; true groups preserve historical click bits, while shifted groups change some if support exists. Action-token mobility and row RMS need not match. Report support rather than assuming the permutation changes information.

No parameter increase is expected; two-group indexing adds modest measured wall/memory/inference cost relative to existing unrestricted rotation. All four cells execute identical learned modules. Report measured costs rather than inferring an efficiency gain.
falsifiers: A true-stratum contrast no larger than the shifted control, or an effect reversing across routing/repetitions, weakens the historical-click-association account under this recipe. It does not refute all historical-feedback utility.
A true-stratum loss as large as unrestricted rotation despite preserved click bits weakens click-bit sufficiency, and motivates a separate auxiliary-bit or match-support diagnostic.

If shifted membership or action values do not actually change on supported inputs, the contrast is vacuous; do not interpret a null as evidence against feedback utility. If tensor parity/ownership/mask gates fail, stop matched interpretation regardless of AUC.

If differences are only consistent with unmatched action perturbation strength, BF16 or bank averaging/optimization, report unresolved attribution; do not label a routing difference as semantic task specialization.
Restoration with true groups alone, one favorable AUC, or superiority to DIN does not establish a mechanism or novelty. No test outcomes may enter this open proposal.
alternative_explanations: One frozen seed and one pass; no user-cluster bootstrap or tensor parity receipt is currently supplied. Existing candidate_diagnostics are not_requested. Same-seed trajectory differences and BF16 effects cannot establish a population mechanism.

Count matching fixes both group sizes and the number of moved source indices, but not the number of changed action tokens, action-summary RMS or action type frequencies. Record these on training inputs; do not divide AUC by a token-change fraction or call restoration alone decisive.

Shifted groups can coincide with true groups, and homogeneous or singleton groups can be identity interventions. Their observed prevalence is unknown; no raw vocabulary or training batch is exposed here.

Task selection versus bank averaging also changes active effective capacity, gradient mixing and scale despite equal parameter count and bank execution; a routing interaction remains operational evidence, not proof of semantic task specialization.

Official offline historical feedback may include immature delayed feedback; auxiliary targets match user/category/brand within24h and do not establish ad-attributed conversions or production causal value.
